original_question: Determine the sharp regularity of generalized minimal flows within anisotropic function spaces tailored to flow-line geometry.
target_in_paper: Section 6.4, Problem 17: "Determine the true regularity of GM-flows in the framework of anisotropic function spaces," read together with Section 6.3, Definition 6.7 and Problems 14–16.
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the paper's target as a regularity question about generalized minimal flows (GM-flows), and it correctly links that question to anisotropic function spaces adapted to a distinguished geometric direction associated with the flow. It also points in the right direction by emphasizing regularity rather than existence, geometry of flow lines, and a sharpened notion of optimal regularity.
missing_details: The paper's object is specifically a GM-flow, defined in the Yudovich setting: a divergence-free vector field u on a compact analytic Riemannian 2-manifold M such that curl u lies in L^infty(M), and for every w in the weak H^1-closure of the Euler orbit of u one has ||curl w||_{L^2(M)} = ||curl u||_{L^2(M)}.

The ambient setting is two-dimensional: M is a compact analytic Riemannian 2-manifold, with or without analytic boundary. Your draft does not specify dimension, analyticity of the manifold, or the boundary condition context inherited from Section 6.3.
The phrase "generalized minimal flows" should be tied to the exact paper notation GM-flow / GM, not left informal.
The regularity issue is posed inside the Yudovich framework for the 2D Euler flow S_t, using the orbit O(u) and its weak closure; these dynamical definitions are omitted in the draft.

The anisotropy is not arbitrary: Problem 16 specifies larger smoothness in the direction of flow lines, while the GM-flow discussion adds expected analytic structure along vorticity level lines and only finite transverse regularity.

The nearby motivating conjecture is that level lines of vorticity of GM-flows are real-analytic (Problem 14); this is still open in the paper, so the refined question should not treat that analyticity as already proved.
The official formulation says "true regularity" rather than explicitly "sharp regularity"; the paper does not fix a pre-existing scale and ask for a best exponent only.
Problem 17 is narrower than Problem 16: it asks only for the regularity description of GM-flows, not also for existence and uniqueness theorems for ideal hydrodynamics in those spaces.

The paper gives a concrete model for anisotropic spaces in the stationary-flow setting via Definitions 6.3–6.5 and Theorem 6.6; if one mentions such spaces, they should be presented as nearby motivation rather than as the exact formal statement of Problem 17.

No ambient ring/field, homogeneity condition, degree restriction, nilpotency hypothesis, or "for sufficiently large m" quantifier is part of this problem; those data are not applicable here and should not be imported.
refined_question: Let M be a compact analytic Riemannian 2-manifold, with or without analytic boundary, and let YU(M) be the Yudovich space of divergence-free vector fields u on M with curl u in L^infty(M). For the 2D Euler flow S_t on YU(M), call u a generalized minimal flow (GM-flow) if for every w in the weak H^1-closure of its orbit O(u) one has ||curl w||_{L^2(M)} = ||curl u||_{L^2(M)}. Determine the true regularity of GM-flows by identifying the anisotropic function spaces natural to them—spaces with enhanced smoothness along the distinguished flow/level-line direction and only finite transverse regularity—in which GM-flows should be studied.
justification: The draft is aiming at Section 6.4, Problem 17, almost verbatim: the paper asks for the "true regularity of GM-flows" in anisotropic function spaces. To make the question stand alone and remain faithful to the paper, one must import the exact GM-flow definition from Section 6.3, Definition 6.7, including the 2D analytic-manifold and Yudovich setting and the orbit-closure criterion. The phrase about geometry "tailored to flow-line geometry" comes from the immediately preceding Problem 16, which asks for anisotropic spaces with greater smoothness in the direction of flow lines. The nearby context further explains why GM-flows are the intended target: they are expected to have analytic vorticity level lines and finite transverse regularity, but that analyticity is itself only conjectural in Problem 14. I therefore kept the refined question centered on regularity alone and did not broaden it to the existence/uniqueness part of Problem 16, nor did I drift to Brenier generalized flows or arbitrary Euler solutions.
